item.content:encoded:
The tale works because it's an exercise in absurdity and implausibility.

As we all know, SCP-682 can't die because Rule of God1 says so. We have this expectation since we first come onto the site and discover this lizard who just can't die no matter what you throw at him. It's plot armor, and it's the reason why 682 is so popular.

Bright and Kain are characters people are commonly introduced to people in some way or form in various tales. Bright, this researcher stuck in an amulet who inhabits whatever body the amulet is worn on (including animals), and Kain, the researcher who happened to turn into a dog somehow. Plausibly, these two could never work in the Foundation due to what has happened to them, but old site culturre coupled with the fact that both of these characters are well-defined2 has made them popular and let them stick around. They're well-established, and not many people could claim to not know who they are.

So what we have in this tale are defiance of expectations, in the form of SCP-682 dying. Not just him dying, but dying due to drunk driving. The most absurd way for him to die, short of an anvil dropping on his head. Meanwhile, we have a dog and a monkey talking about how a big mutated lizard died due to drunk driving, except that 682 died in the monkey's car. A monkey driving a car. And then this monkey starts a group against Drunk Driving, in the car of theirs that was stolen. This is absolutely absurd and could never happen.

And that's why Bright and Kain are in this tale versus Agents Joe and Schmo.

Footnotes
1. Not just words from God, but the rule. Is this an actual trope? If it isn't, I'm coining it :|
2. Whether they are good is up to you.
